displayName: France — Assemblée nationale (Comptes rendus des débats en séance)
sourceName: Assemblée nationale — "Comptes rendus des débats en séance" (compte rendu intégral / Syceron). Two complementary channels: (1) the official AN website HTML search at www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/{leg}/comptes-rendus/seance, and (2) the official open-data bulk dump "SyceronBrut" (syseron.xml.zip) on data.assemblee-nationale.fr. Secondary/unofficial: nosdeputes.fr (Regards Citoyens) REST+JSON search — real API, but STALE (data ends 2024-06).
protocol: No official machine API. Two verified paths: (A) HTTP GET returning **HTML only** (must be parsed/scraped) at www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/... — server-side rendered, no JSON content negotiation (Accept: application/json still returns text/html; appending /json returns HTTP 500). (B) HTTPS GET of a static ZIP-of-XML bulk dump (application/zip, 55.7 MB for leg. 17) from data.assemblee-nationale.fr. Secondary nosdeputes.fr is a genuine REST/JSON API (?format=json) but its debate corpus stops at June 2024.
auth: none — all endpoints verified anonymously with plain curl, no key, no token, no registration, no cookie required. Licence: "Licence Ouverte / Open Licence" (Etalab) for data.assemblee-nationale.fr. nosdeputes.fr: content CC-BY-SA, data ODbL, attribution to NosDéputés.fr / Regards Citoyens + Assemblée nationale required.
searchEndpoint: GET /dyn/{legislature}/comptes-rendus/seance  (HTML search over sitting transcripts; {legislature} is a PATH segment: 17, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11 — the `legislature` form field is NOT honoured as a query param). Companion endpoints: GET /dyn/{legislature}/comptes-rendus/seance/{session-slug}/{sitting-slug} (one full transcript, all speeches inline), same path + `.pdf` (verified 200, application/pdf), GET /dyn/embed/journee-de-comptes-rendus-de-seance?date=DD/MM/YYYY (sittings for one calendar day), GET /dyn/embed/acteur-info-card/{acteurUid}?date=YYYY-MM-DD%20HH:MM:SS (speaker's party group as of that sitting date). Bulk: GET /static/openData/repository/{17|16|15}/vp/syceronbrut/syseron.xml.zip on data.assemblee-nationale.fr.
verificationNote: All of the following was executed live with curl/WebFetch on 2026-08-03. (1) The example request returned HTTP 200, 1,925,104 bytes of HTML, with the literal pagination string "Page n°2 : 36 comptes rendus affichés sur un total de 425", day headers "Mercredi 03 juin 2026 / Mardi 02 juin 2026 / Lundi 01 juin 2026" and docIds CRSANR5L17S2026O1N261, CRSANR5L17S2026O1N259, CRSANR5L17S2026O1N257. Page 1 of the same query returned a DIFFERENT set (CRSANR5L17S2026E1N023/N024/N021, "Mardi 21 juillet 2026"), and page=12 returned "Page n°12 : 24 ... sur un total de 425" — so `page` genuinely pages. (2) `text` genuinely filters full speech text: no filter = 608 total, text=climat = 425, text=bornes+de+recharge = 39 (and the returned set includes the 21 July 2026 sitting whose transcript does contain "Tarifs aux bornes de recharge électrique"), text=zzzqxwv = zero-results page. (3) `depute` filters: depute=PA795228 -> 103; text=climat&depute=PA795228 -> 73. Deputy option values are AN acteur UIDs harvested from the form's

queryParams.note: AN /dyn search. VERIFIED to search the spoken content of transcripts, not just titles: no-filter 608 -> text=climat 425 -> text=bornes+de+recharge 39 -> text=zzzqxwv 0. Space-separated terms are AND-ish; quoting (%22taxe+carbone%22) parses without error. Matches are at SITTING granularity — the response tells you which comptes rendus contain the term, NOT which individual speech. No snippet/highlight is returned (zero <mark> or 'highlight' nodes in the HTML).

Value MUST be an AN acteur UID of the form PA###### (e.g. PA795228), NOT a name. Harvest the full 577-entry mapping from the <select name="depute"> options on the search page itself (<option value="PA795228">Nadège Abomangoli</option>). VERIFIED: depute=PA795228 -> 103 sittings; combines with text (text=climat&depute=PA795228 -> 73).

Legislature is the {leg} PATH segment: /dyn/17/... /dyn/16/... etc. VERIFIED /dyn/16/comptes-rendus/seance?text=climat -> 460 totals, distinct from leg 17's 425. The form's `legislature` field is NOT honoured as a query string param (legislature=16&text=climat on the /dyn/17/ path still returned 425). Iterate the path to cover 17,16,15,14,13,12,11.
1-based. THE ONLY WORKING PAGINATION KNOB. VERIFIED to return disjoint result sets across page=1/2/12.

There is NO date-range parameter anywhere. `seance_date` on the search endpoint is INERT (verified across 8 format variants — all returned unfiltered totals). The only working date filter is the separate single-day embed: /dyn/embed/journee-de-comptes-rendus-de-seance?date=DD/MM/YYYY. Format is strictly DD/MM/YYYY (21/07/2026 -> 86,783 B with links; 2026-07-21 -> 478 B, empty). To emulate a range you must loop day-by-day, or (far better) date-filter locally after ingesting the bulk XML, whose <dateSeance> is an exact timestamp.
UNSUPPORTED server-side. Filter on <dateSeance>/<dateSeanceJour> from the Syceron XML after ingestion, or on the date embedded in the sitting slug (…-du-mardi-21-juillet-2026).
This source is Assemblée nationale only (<typeAssemblee>AN</typeAssemblee>). The Sénat is an entirely separate estate (senat.fr / nossenateurs.fr) and is out of scope for this profile.
PRESENT IN THE SITE'S OWN PAGINATION LINKS BUT INERT. Verified limit=5 and limit=100 both still render 36 comptes rendus per page. Hardcode 36 items/page in the crawler; do not rely on limit.

Distinct from `text` (note the trailing 'e'). A <select> of numbered legislative dossiers (e.g. '3007 - Projet de loi …') that restricts results to sittings examining that bill. Useful for dossier-scoped debate retrieval; not a free-text field.

pagination: AN /dyn HTML search: classic 1-based page-number pagination via `&page=N`. Page size is FIXED at 36 comptes rendus (the `limit` param appears in the site's own generated links but is inert — verified limit=5 and limit=100 both still return 36). Total count is only available by regexing the rendered string `Page n°(\d+) : (\d+) comptes rendus affichés sur un total de (\d+)` (observed: "Page n°2 : 36 comptes rendus affichés sur un total de 425"); last page number is also present in the .an-pagination block as the highest `?…&page=N` href. Compute pages = ceil(total/36). Terminate on the zero-results page (contains "aucun", and no `data-id="CRS…"` nodes). Bulk dump: not paginated — one 55.7 MB ZIP per legislature containing 601 per-sitting XML files; re-fetch and diff on `last-modified` (updated nightly, observed 02:05 UTC) or on the MD5 published alongside it. nosdeputes.fr (stale): proper API pagination — `start`, `end`, `last_result` in the JSON body, `&count=` up to 500 (default 50), `&page=N` yielding items count*(N-1)+1 … count*N.

fieldMapping.sourcePath: XML: /compteRendu/uid  |  HTML: data-id attribute on the result tile, prefix before ' / Bloc de style'
fieldMapping.note: VERIFIED identical across both channels, e.g. 'CRSANR5L17S2026E1N023'. Self-describing: CRS + ANR5 (Ve République AN) + L17 (legislature) + S2026 (session year) + E1/O1 (Extraordinaire/Ordinaire session #) + N023 (sitting number). This is your stable primary key and it is also the ZIP member filename (xml/compteRendu/CRSANR5L17S2026E1N023.xml), which lets you join HTML search hits straight to bulk XML with no extra fetch. For speech-level granularity use the composite docId + '#' + paragraphe/@id_syceron (e.g. CRSANR5L17S2026E1N023#4166230).

fieldMapping.sourcePath: XML: /compteRendu/contenu//paragraphe/orateurs/orateur/nom (+ /orateur/id, + paragraphe/@id_acteur)  |  HTML: p.orateur > span text
fieldMapping.note: VERIFIED real values: <nom>Mme Edwige Diaz</nom><id>793928</id>, on a <paragraphe id_acteur="PA793928">. Note the two ID forms differ only by the 'PA' prefix — orateur/id is the bare numeric (793928) while @id_acteur is the canonical acteur UID (PA793928); normalise to the PA form to join against the AMO deputy datasets and the `depute` search param. Includes the chair as the generic 'Mme la présidente' (id 721908) and interrupters (short heckles are their own <paragraphe>). 650 of 679 paragraphes in the sampled sitting carried an id_acteur; the 29 without are procedural/stage-direction lines (<italique>(La séance est ouverte à quinze heures.)</italique>) which you should drop. Ministers additionally carry <qualite> (e.g. 'ministre de l'Europe et des affaires étrangères') and appear wrapped in <interExtraction nom_orateur=… qualite=… id_acteur=…>. paragraphe/@roledebat='president' flags the chair.

fieldMapping.sourcePath:
XML: /compteRendu/contenu//paragraphe/texte | HTML: the

immediately following div.crs-inter > p.orateur
fieldMapping.note:
This is the FULL verbatim text of one contribution, not a snippet — derive your own snippet by truncating, since neither channel returns keyword-highlighted excerpts (zero /highlight nodes verified). Contains inline markup you must handle:
(paragraph breaks within one speech), (stage directions / applause), / (ordinals like 'article 1er'), and (cross-references to amendments). Uses French typographic apostrophes (U+2019) — normalise before indexing or free-text search will miss terms. Caveat from the AN itself: 'Le compte rendu intégral n'est pas un mot à mot mais la transposition en langage écrit d'interventions orales' — it is an edited verbatim, and speakers have 3 days to request formal corrections.

VERIFIED '20260721150000000' — a 17-char timestamp, NOT ISO: YYYYMMDDHHmmssSSS. Parse as date=20260721, time=15:00:00. dateSeanceJour is the French human form 'mardi 21 juillet 2026'. In the HTML channel the date is only available as the French day header (

Mardi 21 juillet 2026

) or parsed out of the sitting slug (premiere-seance-du-mardi-21-juillet-2026) — both require French month-name parsing, which is a strong argument for using the XML as the metadata source of record.

Two useful levels. Sitting-level title: <journee>Première séance du mardi 21 juillet 2026</journee>. Debate-item title (the one users actually want): titreStruct/intitule under //point or //sommaire2, e.g. 'Questions au gouvernement', 'Visas délivrés aux ressortissants algériens', 'Tarifs aux bornes de recharge électrique'. point/@nivpoint gives the heading depth (1 = top, 2 = sub) so you can build the agenda hierarchy; the <sommaire> block in metadonnees mirrors the same tree with sommaire1/sommaire2/sommaire3 + <para id_syceron> pointing at each speech. Recommended: title = nearest ancestor titreStruct/intitule of the paragraphe.

VERIFIED sessionRef='SCR5A2026E1', seanceRef='RUANR5L17S2026IDS30880' (the sitting's reunion UID, joinable to the AN 'Réunions' dataset), session='Première session extraordinaire 2026', numSeance=23 (nth sitting of the session), numSeanceJour=1 (nth sitting that calendar day). In the HTML channel the session appears only as a URL slug ('session-extraordinaire-de-2025-2026').

VERIFIED '17'. Bulk dumps confirmed available for 17 (55.7 MB), 16 (57.6 MB) and 15 (149 MB); leg 14 returns 404, so pre-2017 debates are HTML/PDF-only via /dyn/14/… and archives.assemblee-nationale.fr. Leg-17 XML covers 2024-07-18 to 2026-07-21 (sampled).
VERIFIED constant 'AN'. Map to a fixed 'Assemblée nationale' / lower house. No upper-house content is ever present in this source.

fieldMapping.sourcePath: HTML: a.link[href] on the result tile → /dyn/{leg}/comptes-rendus/seance/{session-slug}/{sitting-slug}, plus '#' + paragraphe/@id_syceron for the exact speech
fieldMapping.note: NOT PRESENT IN THE XML — the XML gives you uid + id_syceron but no URL, and there is no published uid→slug resolver, so you MUST scrape the HTML index (or the journee embed) at least once per sitting to learn its slug and persist a uid↔slug map. Deep links are verified real: the page ships a per-speech share widget whose data-clipboardText is exactly https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/comptes-rendus/seance/session-extraordinaire-de-2025-2026/premiere-seance-du-mardi-21-juillet-2026#4167762, i.e. anchor == paragraphe/@id_syceron == div.crs-inter@id == data-crs-syceron-id. Append '.pdf' to the same path for the official PDF (verified 200, 704,997 bytes).

fieldMapping.sourcePath: NOT in the debate XML — resolve via GET /dyn/embed/acteur-info-card/{id_acteur}?date=YYYY-MM-DD%20HH:MM:SS, or offline via the AMO10/AMO40 organe+mandat datasets keyed on id_acteur/id_mandat
fieldMapping.note: BIGGEST GAP. The Syceron XML has <qualite> (ministerial title) but NO political group on the speaker; I verified no group/party element exists on <orateur>. Verified workaround: the embed https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/embed/acteur-info-card/PA840817?date=2026-07-21%2015:00:00 returns 200/1,048 bytes reading 'À la date de la séance : M. Joël Bruneau Membre du groupe Libertés, Indépendants, Outre-mer et Territoires' — note it is DATE-SCOPED, which is exactly right for France where deputies change groups mid-term. Doing this per speech is far too many requests; instead build an offline (id_acteur × date-interval → groupe) table from data.assemblee-nationale.fr/static/openData/repository/17/amo/deputes_actifs_mandats_actifs_organes/AMO10_deputes_actifs_mandats_actifs_organes.json.zip (JSON, verified listed) and use the embed only as a fallback. Cheap partial shortcut: the sitting page's own <a class="crs-sommaire-para"> entries carry the group inline for major speakers, e.g. 'M. Arnaud Saint-Martin (LFI-NFP)', 'M. Arthur Delaporte (SOC)', 'Mme Anne Genetet (EPR)' — but only in the sommaire, not on every speech.

French only. The open-data metadata declares Language: fr. No English or other-language debate transcripts exist. Consequence for us: the free-text `text` param and any local index must handle French diacritics, elision apostrophes (U+2019 'l'article'), and the fact that nosdeputes.fr's parlementaire tag requires accents STRIPPED while AN's `text` does not.

fullTextAccess:
The actual spoken words are fully available through two verified channels, and BOTH are needed. (1) BULK XML — the canonical, structured, speech-level source. data.assemblee-nationale.fr/static/openData/repository/17/vp/syceronbrut/syseron.xml.zip: 55.7 MB ZIP -> 601 per-sitting XML files, 324 MB uncompressed, one file per compte rendu named by uid. Each file is a full sitting: metadonnees (date, legislature, session, sitting numbers) + a tree of / where every is one contribution carrying / and the verbatim . 679 paragraphes in the sitting I parsed. This is the only channel that gives you speaker-attributed, individually-addressable speeches as data. Refreshed nightly (last-modified 2026-08-03 02:05 UTC). Note per-document XML fetch by uid is NOT possible (404) — the ZIP is all-or-nothing, so ingest once then diff. (2) HTML transcript pages — same text, server-rendered, one page per sitting (2.8 MB for the one I fetched), with speeches wrapped as

…speaker…

…

…verbatim…

. Needed anyway because it is the ONLY place the public sourceUrl slug exists. (3) Official PDF per sitting (same path + .pdf, verified 200) — presentation-only, do not parse. Recommended architecture: hydrate the corpus from the bulk XML (all text, speakers, dates, structure), scrape the HTML index once per sitting purely to capture the uid→slug mapping for citation URLs, and build your own search index (OpenSearch/pgvector) locally — do NOT put the AN HTML search on a user-facing hot path. Coverage: leg 17 XML spans 2024-07-18 to 2026-07-21; leg 16 and 15 dumps also available; leg 14 and earlier are HTML/PDF-only.
languages: French (fr) exclusively — declared as Language: fr in the open-data metadata and confirmed in every payload. No multilingual or English versions of debate transcripts. Text uses French typographic apostrophes (U+2019) and accented characters; XML is UTF-8 encoded (declared <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>). Normalise apostrophes and consider accent-folding in your index.
rateLimits: No documented rate limit, no quota headers, and no auth — but also no contract, because these are a public website and a static file, not an API. robots.txt on www.assemblee-nationale.fr was fetched and verified to contain NO Disallow for /dyn/ or /comptes-rendus/ and NO Crawl-delay directive (its Disallow list targets legacy /12//13/ paths, /video/, /boutique/, /juniors/ and /opendata/). Treat the absence of limits as fragile, not as permission: HTML search pages are 1.9–2.8 MB each, so a full leg-17 crawl at 36 results/page is ~17 pages per query and ~601 transcript pages at ~2.8 MB = ~1.7 GB. Self-throttle to roughly 1 req/sec with a descriptive User-Agent and a contact URL, cache aggressively, and prefer the single 55.7 MB nightly ZIP over crawling — one ZIP replaces the entire text corpus. Fetch the ZIP at most once daily (it is regenerated ~02:05 UTC) and short-circuit on last-modified / the published MD5.
gotchas: NO OFFICIAL QUERYABLE DEBATES API EXISTS. data.assemblee-nationale.fr is a static-file portal only — I fetched the homepage and the debates page and found no REST, no OData, no SPARQL, and no API documentation anywhere; /api returns 404. Anything that looks like an 'AN API' in the wild is a third-party wrapper (ParlAPI.fr, Tricoteuses GraphQL), not official.

The AN search returns HTML ONLY. Accept: application/json still returns text/html, and appending /json returns HTTP 500. Any Lambda must ship an HTML parser and will break whenever the AN redesigns its templates. This is the single biggest reason the verdict is 'hard' and not 'workable'.

`seance_date` IS A TRAP. It is a real field in the search form (I read it out of the raw HTML) but it is completely INERT as a query parameter — I tried 2026-07-21, 21/07/2026, 20260721, ISO datetime, ' - ' and ' au ' ranges, and [from]/[to] bracket syntax, and every single one returned the unfiltered total (608 unfiltered / 425 with text=climat). If you wire this up assuming it filters, you will silently serve unfiltered results. The real date filter lives at a different endpoint (/dyn/embed/journee-de-comptes-rendus-de-seance?date=DD/MM/YYYY) and only accepts ONE DAY, in DD/MM/YYYY — the ISO form returns 200 with an empty body, which is a second silent-failure trap.

THERE IS NO DATE-RANGE QUERY AT ALL on the official source. Do not design an API contract that promises server-side dateFrom/dateTo. You must either loop the single-day embed or (correct answer) filter locally on <dateSeance> after ingesting the bulk XML.

`limit` is inert too — it appears in the site's OWN pagination hrefs (?text=climat&limit=5&page=2) yet page size stays 36 whether you send 5 or 100. Hardcode 36; never compute page counts from your requested limit.
`legislature` is a path segment, not a query param. Sending ?legislature=16 to /dyn/17/... is silently ignored (still returned leg-17's 425). You must vary the PATH.

Search granularity is the SITTING, not the speech. text=climat tells you 425 comptes rendus mention climate; it does NOT tell you which of the ~679 speeches in each. And no snippets/highlights are returned (zero <mark> nodes). To answer 'who said X' you must ingest the XML and index speech-by-speech yourself — the AN search alone cannot power a speech-level product.

`depute` needs a PA###### acteur UID, not a name. There is no name-based lookup on the search endpoint, so you must first scrape the 577 <option value="PA…">Name</option> pairs off the search page and maintain that map per legislature.
Beware the near-homonym params `text` (free-text keywords) vs `texte` (a dossier/bill selector). A typo silently changes the semantics of the query.

PARTY IS ABSENT from the debate XML. <orateur> has nom/id/qualite but no group; I verified no party element exists. You must join to the AMO10/AMO40 mandate+organe datasets, or call /dyn/embed/acteur-info-card/{PA…}?date=… per speaker. Critically, French deputies switch groups mid-term, so party MUST be resolved as-of the sitting date — the embed is explicitly date-scoped ('À la date de la séance : …'). A naive current-party join will mislabel historical speeches.

Per-sitting XML is NOT individually fetchable by uid (404). It is one 55.7 MB monolithic ZIP per legislature (324 MB uncompressed, 601 files) — too big for a modest Lambda's /tmp plus in-memory parse. Ingest it in a batch/Fargate job or stream ZIP members, not in a request-path Lambda.

The XML has no sourceUrl. It gives uid + id_syceron, but the public URL needs the {session-slug}/{sitting-slug} pair which exists ONLY in the HTML. There is no uid→slug resolver, so you cannot produce citation links from the bulk data alone — you must scrape and persist the mapping.
dateSeance is NOT ISO. '20260721150000000' is YYYYMMDDHHmmssSSS (17 chars). Feeding it to a standard date parser will throw or, worse, misparse.

In the HTML channel dates appear only as French text ('Mardi 21 juillet 2026') or inside slugs ('premiere-seance-du-mardi-21-juillet-2026'), requiring French month-name parsing. Another reason to treat the XML as the metadata source of record.

NOSDEPUTES.FR IS STALE — DO NOT BUILD ON IT. It is genuinely the nicest API here (clean REST, ?format=json, real free-text + date-range + speaker filters, proper start/end/last_result pagination) and it is tempting, but I proved its debate corpus ENDS 2024-06: timefacet buckets are non-zero only from 202206 to 202406, and a 2025-06-01→2026-08-03 date query returned last_result:0. It has ZERO coverage of the current 17th legislature. Its filters return HTTP 200 with empty results rather than erroring, so a naive integration would look healthy while serving nothing.

nosdeputes.fr quirks if you use it for the 16th legislature or earlier: ?format=xml returns HTTP 500 (JSON only, despite the docs); the documented /recherche/{q}/json path-suffix form returns an empty {} while only ?format=json works; /{leg}/seance/{id}/json returned HTTP 500 on the ids I tried; and the &tag=parlementaire= filter requires accents and cedillas STRIPPED with spaces as '+'. Archived per-legislature hosts (2017-2022.nosdeputes.fr) do respond.

The compte rendu is an EDITED verbatim, not a literal transcript — the AN states 'Le compte rendu intégral n'est pas un mot à mot mais la transposition en langage écrit d'interventions orales', and speakers get 3 days to request formal corrections. Also <version>avant_JO</version> marks pre-Journal-Officiel text that can still change, so recent sittings are mutable — re-ingest recent dates rather than treating first fetch as final.

Non-speech noise in the XML: ~29 of 679 paragraphes have no id_acteur and are stage directions/procedural lines (<italique>(La séance est ouverte à quinze heures.)</italique>); short heckles are their own paragraphes; the chair appears as generic 'Mme la présidente'; and <changementPresidence> mid-sitting means the chair identity changes within one document. Filter and attribute carefully or your speech counts and speaker stats will be wrong.

Legislature coverage cliff: bulk XML exists for 17, 16, 15 only — leg 14's syseron.xml.zip is a hard 404. Pre-2017 debates are HTML/PDF only (and older ones live on archives.assemblee-nationale.fr), so any 'search all French debates ever' promise is not deliverable from this source.

Scope note as instructed: Legifrance/PISTE was NOT researched — it is statute text and out of scope. Also explicitly out of scope from this portal: /travaux-parlementaires/votes (voting records), /amendements, and /dossiers (bill tracking). The Sénat is a separate institution with a separate estate (senat.fr / nossenateurs.fr) and is not covered here.
